questions.prompt: What makes a graph a LINE graph?
questions.explanation: A line graph connects its data points with line segments.
questions.misconception: Bars make a bar chart and a single dot is a data point — the connecting line is the signature of a line graph.

questions.prompt: What does each DOT on a line graph represent?
questions.explanation: Each dot is one measured data point at a specific time.
questions.misconception: Dots are individual observations, not averages or bars — the line then connects them into a trend.

questions.prompt: If the line on a graph goes DOWN from left to right, the values are...
questions.explanation: A downward line means later values are lower — decreasing.
questions.misconception: Left-to-right motion follows time, and lower dots on the right mean smaller values — decreasing.

questions.prompt: On a line graph of temperature by hour, the time is shown...
questions.explanation: Time runs along the horizontal axis from left to right.
questions.misconception: The vertical axis holds the measured values (temperature); time is the horizontal sequence.

questions.prompt: When is a line graph better than a bar chart?
options: When you want to show a trend over time
questions.explanation: The connecting line reveals trends and direction of change — exactly what time data needs.
questions.misconception: Comparing distinct categories is the bar chart's strength; the line exists to reveal the trend.
